products.title: Kenya Konyu AB
products.body_html:
Konyu AB is a fully washed Kenyan coffee grown by farmers who are part of the Kabare Society, which operates 10 factories and has nearly 14,000 members. Farms are located throughout the Kirinyaga region, which is situated just south of Mount Kenya, the second-highest peak in Africa. The coffee varieties grown—SL 28, SL 34, Ruiru 11, and Batian—thrive in the region’s high elevation (around 1,800 meters) and benefit from its nutrient-rich volcanic soil.

Cherries are handpicked and pulped upon delivery to the washing station. Fermentation typically lasts 14-16 hours. Once the mucilage is fully broken down, the coffee is moved to raised beds where it is gently dried over the course of 14-21 days.

products.title: Honduras Caballero Pacamara Natural
products.body_html: Everything about this coffee is big. The Pacamara variety produces big cherries, big seeds, and big flavors, and it was produced by one the biggest names in Honduran coffee: the Caballero family. Having worked with the Caballeros since 2002, we have featured many lots from their award-winning farm, but they never cease to offer something new. This lot marks our first release of the naturally processed Pacamara, which takes the notes of this already fruit-forward cultivar and ups the intensity.

products.title: Costa Rica Calle Copey Honey
products.body_html:
Our second Costa Rican release of the year comes from our long-time Direct Trade partners at Coopedota, a farmer cooperative in Dota, San José, renowned for bringing some of the country's best coffees to market. Our partnership started in 2005, and we have continued to receive excellent coffee year after year. With a history of being at the forefront of innovation, each lot we source is processed at Coopedota's carbon-neutral mill.

During our visit earlier this year, this particular lot stood out: a blend of Caturra and Catuaí grown by eight neighboring farmers and processed in the honey style, which leaves more of the coffee pulp intact during the washing and drying phases. The resulting cup is full of lasting and complex sweetness.

products.title: Honduras El Ocotal
products.body_html: Brought to us by our partners at Bon Café, this lot is a single-farm selection from Juan Pascual's El Ocotal in La Laguna, Lempira. This is our first year sourcing from Juan Pascual and this release marks our first of the season from Honduras. It stood out for its sweetness, balance, and complexity.

products.title: Guatemala Las Moritas SOE
products.body_html: The diverse terrain, soil, and microclimates of Las Moritas result in sweet, complex coffees that help anchor both our blends and our single origin menu.

products.title: Peru El Romerillo
products.body_html:
This lot is a blend of washed Caturra, Pache, and Catimor varietals grown by Micaela Peña at her farm, El Romerillo, in La Coipa, San Ignacio. It was sourced in collaboration with the team at Origin Coffee Lab, who have been helping us identify the best coffees from Peru's northern highlands for nearly ten years.

Micaela is a member of Origin Coffee Lab's El Horcón committee of producers. The committee structure brings together producers who might otherwise be isolated, enabling them to share best practices, with Origin Coffee Lab providing crucial access and insights to and from the international market. Micaela's farm, El Romerillo, spans one hectare, but together with her committee members, they are cultivating over seven varieties of coffee on more than twenty hectares of land.

products.title: Costa Rica Coopedota
products.body_html: Our first Costa Rica release of the year comes from our longtime Direct Trade partners at Coopedota, a farmer cooperative in Santa María de Dota, Tarrazú that has been producing some of Costa Rica’s finest coffees since 1960 and collaborating with Intelligentsia since 2005.

products.title: Colombia El Estoraque Honey
products.body_html:
Yeison Libardo López comes from a long line of coffee growers. He is continuing the legacy of the generations before him on his farm, El Estoraque, in the town of Buesaco, Nariño. Perched atop a ridge of the Colombian Andes in the storied state of Nariño, Buesaco is a specialty coffee hub that is renowned for its quality. The combination of high altitude (averaging 2,000 meters), volcanic soils, and a climate of warm days, cool nights, and distinct rainy and dry seasons, creates the ideal conditions for growing coffee. With the right knowledge and infrastructure, coffee producers like Don Yeison can capitalize on these natural conditions, preparing lots that highlight the best of what Buesaco's terroir has to offer.

Diverging from the tradition of washed coffees, this lot is a honey process. After the ripe cherries were harvested, the coffee was de-pulped just enough to remove the skin while still leaving some of the pulpy fruit in tact. From there, the coffee was fermented anaerobically for an extended period of time, and washed just once before being transferred to covered, raised drying beds. The extended fermentation combined with the presence of the fruit pulp imparts a tangy sweetness to the coffee while still presenting a cup with balance and clarity.

products.title: Colombia Peña Blanca
products.body_html:
Origin Story

Peña Blanca is a small farm tucked into a northern pocket of the acclaimed coffee-growing region of Nariño. Before becoming a coffee farmer, Enuar Rodrigo Ramos raised livestock. He then used his proceeds to build a home for his family and acquire a 2-hectare plot of land dedicated to coffee. This lot is harvested from the Colombia Variety trees that Don Enuar cultivates on his farm.

The Colombia Variety is the result of a laboratory cross between Caturra and Timor Hybrid, yielding a plant that is resistant to coffee leaf rust, produces high cup quality, and can be densely planted to allow for more efficient and productive harvests. While this variety can be found on farms throughout Colombia, the care that Don Enuar and his family take in harvesting only ripe cherries and drying the coffee on covered, raised beds yields exceptional results.

products.title: Burundi Yandaro Natural
products.body_html: Over the past eight seasons, our search for the cleanest and sweetest coffees in Burundi has led us to the village of Yandaro, where Greenco purchases and processes ripe cherry from thousands of smallholder farmers and processes it with an exacting focus on quality. Each year, our coffee team looks forward to launching Yandaro lots on our single origin menu. This lot, a carefully processed natural, offers a surprising twist on the traditional washed coffees we typically offer from Burundi. The resulting cup delivers notes of ripe dark fruits and the deep, syrupy sweetness of a fortified wine.

products.title: Colombia San Miguel Castillo
products.body_html:
Francy Elena Rivera Quiñonez began helping her husband on their coffee farm in central Cauca 13 years ago. In 2017, with hopes of increasing opportunities for her family, Dona Francy acquired her own one-hectare plot of land, San Miguel. She restored the land and began planting coffee, eventually producing enough to sell it on her own. The additional income from her farm has allowed the family to build a home and invest in an education for their son.

This lot is a selection of Castillo cherries, a variety that is resistant to coffee leaf rust and was introduced to Colombian farmers in 2005 — it is now the most commonly planted variety in the country. Over time, smallholder producers like Dona Francy have helped improve the quality perception of Castillo by selectively picking only the ripest, deep-red cherries and processing the coffee with meticulous care.

Shot specs: 18g in / 46-48g out / 33-35 seconds

products.title: Colombia Las Cruces Caturra Chiroso
products.body_html:
As a teenager, Yolanda María Gómez ventured away from the coffeelands, moving to the city where she settled into her new life, building a career and starting a family. It was only after her daughter, Julieth, graduated from high school and began working as a coffee cupper that Yolanda felt the pull back to her coffee roots. Inspired by her daughter's passion and knowledge of specialty coffee, Yolanda returned to El Arenal in San Pedro de Cartago, Nariño, to farm on Las Cruces, a one-hectare plot of land she inherited from her mother. With the combined knowledge of three generations of women in coffee, Yolanda began renovating Las Cruces, planting coffee varieties known for their high cup quality that would benefit from the farm's high elevation.

This lot is a selection from Caturra Chiroso plants that Yolanda planted on Las Cruces just four years ago, making this one of the first harvests these plants will produce. Though the exact origins and genetic makeup of Caturra Chiroso remain undefined, the variety is named for its resemblance to short, compact Caturra plants — yet its cup profile evokes notes more often found in heirloom Ethiopian varieties.

products.title: Colombia San Pedro de Cartago
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This washed Castillo lot was produced by 13 farmers at an elevation of 1,6o0 to 2,000 MASL in the acclaimed region of Nariño in southwestern Colombia. The farmers selectively picked coffee cherries in the fields, floated them to remove insect damaged cherries, and then stored them in wooden hoppers or a plastic tank for 12 to 14 hours. The cherries then passed through the traditional washed process -- after pulping the cherries, the coffee was fermented for 24 to 48 hours (depending on the temperature outside) so that the mucilage could be easily washed off. The coffee was then dried on patios or in parabolic dryers for 15 to 21 days.

The Castillo variety is relatively new -- it was developed by the Colombia National Coffee Research Center, Cenicafé, and released to Colombian farmers in 2005. This variety's popularity has grown quickly due to its resistance to coffee leaf rust, a crippling fungus that spreads when it rains. Intelligentsia was a charter member of the Advisory Council for the Borderlands project which helped farmers validate that the quality of the new Castillo variety was similar to the Caturra variety which it is often replacing.

As always, our roasting approach to this coffee is to maximize sweetness and fruit acids. A great starting point for your dial-in is: 18 gram in / 45 grams out / 35 seconds.

Sensory

products.title: Peru Rayos del Sol
products.body_html:
Origin Story

As part of our first wave of single origin releases from the Peru harvest, we are showcasing this coffee from Rayos del Sol. In collaboration with our Direct Trade partners at Origin Coffee Lab, we have worked with this farm since 2015 and have seen their quality evolve year after year. This coffee is produced by Percy Pintado of the Pintado family, whose farms neighbor each other in Alto Ihuamaca, a small town nestled between two forest conservation areas in the Cajamarca region of Peru’s northern highlands. Rayos del Sol has continued to offer sweet and elegant coffees, with this year’s selection being no exception.

Sensory

products.title: Rwanda Murundo Kivubelt
products.body_html:

This marks our second release of the year from Kivubelt Coffee, which is owned and operated by our Direct Trade partner Furaha Umwizeye. Located in the Nyamasheke district of western Rwanda, this coffee comes from a group of smallholder farmers, collectively known as People’s Farm.

Sensory

products.title: Kenya Kii AA
products.body_html:
Origin Story

The Kii coffee factory is run by a cooperative of 850 active members in the Kirinyaga region of Kenya. Located at the base of Mt. Kenya which is the second-highest peak in Africa, this coffee factory is named after the Kii river that flows nearby. The Kii coffee factory team receives coffee cherries from its members and then sort, float, depulp, ferment, wash, and soak the coffee. The coffee is then dried for two week on raised beds before it is precisely milled to the Kenyan AA grade classification. The dry milling ensures a uniform coffee bean size which we've found enhances the acidity and expressiveness of the tasting notes.

Sensory

Our last Kenyan coffee offering of the season is steadily sweet and juicy with a stone fruit base, and grapefruit acidity to make it a truly rounded cup of coffee.

products.title: Rwanda Jarama Kivubelt
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This coffee comes from farmers near Kivubelt's Jarama Coffee Washing Station in the Nyamasheke district, Western Province of Rwanda. They are known collectively as the "People's Farm”, a collaboration of hundreds of small-scale family farmers.

Sensory

The first single origin release of two from Kivubelt in Rwanda comes from the Jarama washing station, and articulates the sweet yet tart profile that makes Central African coffees a standout.

products.title: Peru Marañón River Valley
products.body_html:
Origin Story

For several years, Asociación de Productores Cafetaleros de la Cuenca del Rio Marañón (APROCCURMA) has been working directly with 124 women producers to establish coffee production from farms owned and managed by women. The cooperative also provides producers with financing, training, and technical assistance to improve coffee quality. They strive to improve the quality of life for coffee producers and their families and gain improved premiums based on a reputation for quality.

Sensory

This Peruvian coffee is an approachable cup, with its confectionary like sweetness and notes of dried fruit.

products.title: Kenya Gititu
products.body_html:
Origin Story

The Gititu Farmers Cooperative Society celebrates the 70th anniversary of its founding next year. With more than 5,000 members and eight coffee washing stations, it is one of the most formidable in all of Kenya. Bright top notes of passionfruit are laid over mellow caramelized sugar in this sparkling lot.

Sensory

This coffee embodies the idea of taste of place, with its intense tropical fruits melding beautifully with sweet and juicy stone fruits.

products.title: Kenya Weithaga
products.body_html:
Origin Story

Weithaga AA represents the work of over 800 smallholder producers and demonstrates the most precise milling protocols exported from Kenya. The coffee is grown in the Aberdare Mountain range which has ideal growing conditions.

We purchased this lot with the help of Mbula Musau of Utake Coffee and BD Imports. After identifying this coffee at Mbula’s lab in spring 2023 during a blind cupping, we kept a close watch on the auction on a nearby screen. The auction refers to the Nairobi Coffee Exchange where nearly all coffee passes on its way to being exported. This buying model is unique and one of the ways that Kenyan farmers are rewarded for the quality of their harvest.

Sensory

Juicy citrus and stone fruit are the base of this vibrant coffee from Kenya, and we are excited to share it this holiday season!

products.title: Ethiopia Natural Yirgacheffe
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This lot is uncommon: it comes from a single small-scale grower in Ethiopia, where most people's small daily harvests are bulked with others to create larger lots. Alemu Beraso's coffee was separated from the rest of the coffee at the washing station where it was processed, then dried in the fruit to create pronounced berry flavors.

products.title: Mexico Finca Chelín Hydronatural Natural
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This lot was grown at Finca Chelín, high in the Sierra Sur of Oaxaca, by Enrique López, a celebrated grower who is among the most experimental coffee farmers in our entire Direct Trade network. It is a single-varietal Geisha, but chances are it won’t taste quite like the last Geisha you tasted. That’s because it is what Enrique calls a “hydronatural natural” lot. Like other naturals, it was dried in the fruit. Unlike other naturals, its slow, four-week drying cycle was interrupted by an overnight soak in cold water at the end of day three. The combination of the coffee’s Geisha genetics, Finca Chelín’s exceptional terroir, and Enrique’s creative processing make this coffee unlike any other Geisha — or any natural — you will taste this year.

products.title: Kenya Gatagua
products.body_html:
Origin Story

Kenya is one of the world's most celebrated coffee origins, thanks in part to the equatorial latitude and soaring elevation of its coffee regions, in part to the intrinsic quality of the SL-28 and SL-34 cultivars that have anchored its coffee fields for the better part of a century, and in part to the way its coffee comes to market. Every harvest, more than a half-million small-scale family farmers across the country deliver freshly harvested coffee cherry to coffee processing centers, known locally as factories, where it is sorted and processed with meticulous care, producing flavors you can’t find anywhere else. We were so excited with what we tasted from this year’s Kenya harvest that we sourced nine different lots. This one, among the best, was grown by members of the Gatagua Farmers Cooperative Society and processed at their factory in Murang’a.

products.title: Mexico Oaxaca Geisha
products.body_html:
Origin Story

We have been sourcing organic coffee from members of Mexican cooperative CEPCO since 2002. Historically, that has meant sourcing the elegant Bourbon and Typica cultivars they grow in the shade of multi-story forest canopies across the rugged mountains of Oaxaca. When the coop raised Geisha seedlings and distributed them to members six years ago, we began working with them on plans to separate their Geisha production from the other varieties they grow. This lot represents the culmination of those efforts, our first smallholder Geisha lot from members of the CEPCO cooperative, but almost certainly not our last.

products.title: El Salvador Malacara SL-28 XF
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This coffee embodies Intelligentsia’s collaborative approach to innovation in the name of quality. Over a decade ago, Malacara’s fourth-generation owner Guillermo “Epe” Álvarez decided to diversify the varieties on his family’s farm to expand the range of flavors it produced. We helped him access SL-28 seed from Kenya and waited patiently for years until it started to bear fruit. We have had the honor of offering it every year since it came into production, and 2023 marks a milestone — 10 years since the first lot of Malacara SL-28. To mark the occasion, we collaborated with Epe in the same spirit of quality-focused innovation that led to the planting of the SL-28 in the first place: we agreed to double the fermentation time from 24 to 48 hours, producing a distinctive cup profile.

Sensory

This extended fermentation version of the SL-28 from El Salvador combines the complexity of Juniper with sweet stone fruit notes - a coffee that is perfect for savoring each sip.

products.title: Kenya Kamviu
products.body_html: Kenya is one of the world's most celebrated coffee origins, thanks in part to the equatorial latitude and soaring elevation of its coffee regions, in part to the intrinsic quality of the SL-28 and SL-34 cultivars that have anchored its coffee fields for the better part of a century, and in part to the way its coffee comes to market. Every harvest, more than a half-million small-scale family farmers across the country deliver freshly harvested coffee cherry to coffee processing centers, known locally as factories, where it is sorted and processed with meticulous care, producing flavors you can’t find anywhere else. We were so excited with what we tasted from this year’s Kenya harvest that we sourced nine different lots. This one, among the largest, was grown by members of the Gakundu Farmers Cooperative Society and processed at their Kamviu factory in Embu, in Kenya's Central Region.

products.title: Colombia Balceros
products.body_html: Huila is the center of gravity in Colombian coffee. It is home to more than 100,000 growers who produce more coffee than any other region, and more than its fair share of the country’s best coffees. Within Huila, San Agustín has emerged as our favorite growing area and the most reliable source of single-origin coffees. We have been working there since 2016 with the exporter In-Conexus and a small but growing number of smallholder farmers committed to producing lots of extraordinary quality, including this one from the Balceros farm of Miller Fabricio Hoyos, who is making his first appearance on our single-origin menu.

products.title: Guatemala La Florida
products.body_html:
Origin Story

In 2020, with help from the nonprofit CRS and funding from USAID, we convened a coffee quality event for smallholder cooperatives in Guatemala that we called Intelligentsia ECWx. We were impressed with the three women who represented the COOPESQUI coop, and even more impressed with the coffee they offered us. We sourced one small lot from them that same year, and never looked back. This is the fourth consecutive year we have worked with COOPESQUI, and the coffee just keeps getting better. This lot, grown by women and sourced from an organization run by women, is the largest of the three single-origin lots we sourced this season from COOPESQUI.

Sensory

The jammy sweetness of this coffee is accentuated by the soft citrus note, and is rounded out by a buttery-like texture akin to a shortbread cookie.

products.title: Costa Rica Santa María
products.body_html: We have been traveling to the rolling hills of Santa María de Dota since 2005, and working with the leadership of the Coopedota cooperative to source the best coffees the region has to offer. This year, after several seasons sourcing exclusively small, single-farm lots of exotic varieties that emphasize the flavors of specific varieties, we added larger, community-based lots of more traditional varieties back into the mix to offer a taste of place.

products.title: Costa Rica Coopedota Women's Lot
products.body_html: Coopedota is a farmer cooperative in Costa Rica that has been bringing some of the country's best coffees to market since 1960 and collaborating with Intelligentsia since 2005. In 2023, Coopedota did something it had never done before — it challenged the 32 women who participate in its microlot program to produce the very best coffees they could, then combined them in its first-ever women's coffees. This lot represents the hard work of 18 of Coopedota's most accomplished female members.

products.title: Burundi Grand Cru Auction Lot
products.body_html: JNP Coffee has been helping us source small lots of exceptional Bourbon from Burundi since 2016. So when it held the country's first-ever private auction late last year, the question wasn't whether we would bid on one of the 26 lots on offer, but which one we would choose. In the end, our coffee team awarded its highest scores to this washed Bourbon lot from Karuzi Province.

products.title: Burundi Kibingo Special Process
products.body_html: An experimental coffee from familiar friends in Burundi.

products.title: Colombia Suspiros
products.body_html: This lot features Tabi, a variety developed by Colombia's National Coffee Research Institute, CENICAFÉ, to boost yields and improve resistance to disease. CENICAFÉ released Tabi to much fanfare in 2002, but then released its Castillo variety just three years later. In less than a decade, the Castillo variety became the most common coffee variety in Colombia, and Tabi was virtually obsolete.. When Libardo Pepicano planted it at his Suspiros farm, he joined a small but growing movement of quality-focused growers who are reviving Tabi for its combination of cup quality, yield, and disease resistance. This lot jumped off the table when we first tasted it in Colombia back in November. We have been eagerly awaiting its arrival ever since.

products.title: Peru La Conquista
products.body_html: This lot is a blend of washed Bourbon and Caturra varietals grown by Nicolás Chilcón Tocto at his farm La Conquista. It was sourced in collaboration with the team at Origin Coffee Lab, which has been helping us identify the best coffees from Cajamarca since 2016.

products.title: Colombia Pink Bourbon
products.body_html:
Origin Story

The Pink Bourbon variety has quickly become one of our coffee team's favorites. When it is grown at the right elevation, harvested at peak ripeness, and meticulously processed, the Pink Bourbon will produce a complex and sweet cup of coffee.

Sensory

This pink bourbon from Colombia is brimming with the complexity we have come to love from this variety - filled with notes of berry and stone fruit that is balanced with tart hibiscus.

products.title: Colombia Juan Martín Geisha
products.body_html: Since 2016, we have been collaborating with the specialty coffee operator Banexport to source coffee from smallholder growers in Cauca. This coffee is something altogether different — a washed Geisha from Finca Juan Martín, an experimental farm where Banexport works to identify the best growing and post-harvest practices for each of the varieties it has planted there.

products.title: Colombia La Lomita Single Origin Espresso
products.body_html:
Our first single origin espresso release of 2023 comes from Hermel Lasso's La Lomita farm in Buesaco, high in the Andes of southern Colombia. The La Lomita single origin espresso is reminiscent of fruit punch with its bounty of ripe stone fruit balanced out by a soft citrus. Its intensity lends itself to being grown at a higher elevation, and helps with clarity in the cup. This single origin espresso presents a fruity alternative to our Black Cat Classic, with notes of ripe stone fruit balanced out by soft citrus. It can be enjoyed with or without milk and is a refreshing summer take on a classic espresso shot.

18g in / 35-37 seconds / 50-52 grams

products.title: Colombia Juan Martín Castillo
products.body_html: Our first-ever single-varietal Castillo release comes from Juan Martín, an experimental farm in Cauca owned and operated by Banexport, which has been plying us with delicious coffee from Cauca since 2016. This coffee was processed using a novel anaerobic fermentation that delivers pronounced berry and dark fruit flavors.

products.title: Black Cat Project Subscription
products.body_html: Subscribe and enjoy a lineup designed for sweetness, cleanliness, and complexity.

products.title: Colombia El Credo
products.body_html: Our first release of the season from Nariño comes from Finca El Credo in Buesaco, where we have been buying coffee since 2010 — our longest-running sourcing project in Colombia.

products.title: Peru El Gallito de la Roca
products.body_html: This lot was grown by Irene Herrera Cabrera and Milciades Minga, two members of the farmer organization Gallito de la Roca. Their farm lies in the crease of a fold in the rugged Peruvian Andes, a long walk up a narrow path from the nearest road, in a community that is a natural habitat for Peru's national bird.

products.title: Intelligentsia Seasonal Select
products.body_html: This seasonally rotating subscription will feature our five seasonal blends that are curated by our coffee team.

products.title: Kenya Gichathaini
products.body_html: The Gichathaini coffee washing station is located in the celebrated coffee region of Nyeri in Central Kenya, and owned and operated by the award-winning Gikanda Farmers Cooperative Society. We have sourced coffee from Gikanda and Gichathaini on and off since 2008.

products.title: Costa Rica La Bandera Geisha
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This Geisha varietal lot was grown by Jesus Ureña Hidalgo at his farm, La Bandera, in the El Congo district high above Santa María de Dota. It was honey-processed by the team at COOPEDOTA, which has been actively promoting exotic varieties like Geisha and helping us separate and source them from individual farms for the past eight seasons.

Sensory

Our third Geisha offering from Costa Rica beautifully illustrates the sweetness that is inherent in this varietal, with a slight zest of candied orange peel to round it out.

products.title: Costa Rica El Congo Geisha
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This tiny lot of Geisha was grown by Efrén Armando Rodríguez Badilla on his farm in the El Congo district, in the hills high above Santa María de Dota. It was honey-processed by the team at COOPEDOTA, which has been actively promoting exotic varieties like Geisha and helping us separate and source them from individual farms for the past eight seasons. It has a honeyed sweetness, flavors of apricot, pear, and orange, and reminds us of Earl Grey tea, with pronounced notes of bergamot.

Sensory

This coffee's delicate Geisha qualities is a pleasant balance in sweetness, with dried fruit and honey to round out the subtle bergamot aftertaste.

products.title: Honduras Caballero Family Experimental
products.body_html: It is no coincidence that the Caballero Family has produced more than 20 winning lots in the Honduras Cup of Excellence competition since 2004 — it is one of the hardest-working and most restlessly innovative families in Honduran coffee. This lot is the result of one of its most recent experiments: freshly harvested coffee cherries are sealed in what the family calls "semi-anaerobic" conditions for three days before resuming the traditional washed process.

products.title: Colombia La Pelota Pink Bourbon
products.body_html: We were introduced to Doña Rovira by our friends at the coffee exporter In-Conexus, which has been supporting our work with a small group of growers in San Agustín since 2016. In 2018, we purchased a handful of single-farm lots from In-Conexus through its Best of Huila competition, including a Pink Bourbon from La Pelota. Since then, La Pelota’s Pink Bourbon has become a perennial favorite of our coffee team, and it appears we are not the only ones who like it: another one of Doña Rovira's Pink Bourbon lots took sixth place at the last Colombia Cup of Excellence competition. We tried that award-winning lot and liked it, but we liked this lot even better.

products.title: Colombia El Diviso
products.body_html: Huila is the center of gravity in Colombian coffee, home to more than 100,000 coffee growers and source of more of the country's best coffees than any other region. Within Huila, San Agustín has emerged as our favorite growing area and the most reliable source of single-origin coffees. This one comes from Blanca Bolaños, who has been growing coffee longer than she can remember on her El Diviso farm.

products.title: Ethiopia Metad Chelbesa Washed
products.body_html: This is what you get when you combine Ethiopia's incomparable terroir and unique heirloom coffee types with meticulous post-harvest processing. This is a smallholder coffee grown in Chelbesa and processed by METAD at its washing station in Gedeb.

products.title: Ethiopia Metad Benti Nenqa Washed
products.body_html: Our collaboration with METAD has anchored our Ethiopia sourcing program since we started working together a decade ago. The return of Benti Nenqa to our single-origin menu for the first time since 2015 brings us full-circle: it was the source of some of the earliest lots we sourced from METAD. This is the first in a series of washed single-origin releases from METAD featuring the best selections of the season.

products.title: Colombia Chachagüí Natural
products.body_html: Intelligentsia doesn't offer many natural-process coffees. In fact, for many years we didn't offer any at all. Since 2016, we have carefully selected a few naturals each year for our single-origin menu, but they have all come from just one country, Ethiopia. Until now. This natural lot from Colombia represents the hard work of three small-scale family farmers in Nariño.

products.title: Rwanda People's Farm
products.body_html: People's Farm isn't a farm at all — it is an ongoing collaboration between a few hundred small-scale family farmers in the remote village of Murundo and Kivubelt Coffee, a local coffee company that provides them with seedlings, helps them improve farm management, and processes their coffee at its washing station there.

products.title: Colombia Sotara Pink Bourbon
products.body_html: In 2016, we began working with a small group of family farmers near Sotará in the southern Colombian region of Cauca committed to improving the quality of their coffee. Since then, their coffee has gotten better, their ranks have grown, and they have embraced the Pink Bourbon cultivar. This lot comes from the El Cabuyal farm of Jaime Sánchez Ledezma.

products.title: Colombia San Antonio
products.body_html: This is our third consecutive single-origin release of the season from Buesaco, and the third from the López family, the most decorated in Colombian coffee. It was grown on Finca San Antonio by Nilson López.

products.title: Colombia Tolima
products.body_html: This organic single-origin coffee comes from Planadas, whose name is Spanish for plains. It is ironic, since the only flat space in Planadas is the small mesa that is home to its quaint downtown and modest landing strip. Beyond lie mountains, rising and falling endlessly in a rugged stretch of the Colombian Andes where this coffee comes from. It was grown by family farmers in three villages as part of the El Paraíso project, an initiative of our friends at the exporter In-Conexus.

products.title: Ethiopia Metad Beriti Washed
products.body_html: The fourth single-origin release of the season from our friends at METAD, this aromatic lot from the storied Yirgacheffe region was grown by smallholders in Beriti and processed at the METAD washing station in Gedeb.

products.title: Honduras Caballero Family Pacamara
products.body_html:
Everything about this coffee is big. The Pacamara variety produces big cherry, big seed, and big flavor, and this lot was produced by the biggest names in Honduran coffee: Moisés Herrera and the Caballero family have won more Cup of Excellence competitions than any other family in the country.

PLEASE NOTE: This coffee roasts & ships from Chicago only.

products.title: Ethiopia Metad Chelchele Washed
products.body_html: This lot is comprised of indigenous Ethiopian varieties grown by smallholders in the Gedeo Zone, whose hallmark floral aromatics, pronounced stone fruit flavors, and relentless sweetness have made the Yirgacheffe name famous. It was processed with meticulous care by the Adinew family at the Metad washing station in Gedeb.

products.title: Intelligentsia Classics
products.body_html: This monthly rotating subscription will send you a different blend every month so you can taste all the classics. This is a great option for those who are new to our coffees or for those who like variety!

products.title: Ethiopia Metad Buku Natural
products.body_html: This lot was dried in the fruit. It delivers the amplified sweetness and abundant dark fruit flavors we expect from a natural-process coffee without muting the intrinsic quality of this heirloom variety or the exceptional terroir of the place where it was grown. Try it with our Ethiopia Metad Buku Washed to see what a difference processing can make.

products.title: Brazil Fazenda Sertão
products.body_html: Over the past quarter-century, Brazilian farmers seeking access to the growing specialty coffee market abandoned the traditional natural process in favor of the newer pulp natural process in the name of increased consistency and quality. Recently, we have seen more quality-focused growers returning to the natural process and applying a new focus on quality to produce consistent and tasty results, like this Yellow Bourbon from the Dias Pereira family's award-winning Fazenda Sertão in Carmo de Minas.

products.title: Brazil Antonio Rigno
products.body_html: Antonio Rigno is among Brazil's most-decorated coffee growers, with three top-10 finishes at the country's Cup of Excellence competition over the past decade. At 70 years old, when many people are enjoying retirement, he still spends part of every day in the field applying the meticulous approach to quality that made his coffee famous.

products.title: Rwanda Busanze
products.body_html: This coffee was processed at the Busanze washing station and grown by members of the KUN cooperative. KUN stands for Koperative Umurego Nteko and means Nteko Cooperative Force. More than half of its members are women, and women feature prominently on the KUN Board of Directors, meaning that force is largely female. This is our second annual single-origin release from KUN and Busanze.

products.title: Colombia El Bado
products.body_html: We traveled to Nariño in 2010 for the Cup of Excellence competition and tasted some unforgettable coffees from Buesaco. We decided to visit to see for ourselves the source of such extraordinary coffee, and we never stopped going back. El Bado was among the first farms in Nariño we sourced from, and it has made regular appearances on our menu ever since.

products.title: Colombia Arcafe
products.body_html:
Arcafé is a farmer association in the far-flung community of Linares in the southern Colombian department of Nariño. When we met them back in 2012 as part of the Borderlands Project of CRS, Linares was better known for its sugarcane than its coffee. Arcafé has helped to change that by generating opportunities for its members through the sale of coffees like this one, from Ana María Caicedo and Pablo Orlando Chavez.

PLEASE NOTE: This coffee roasts & ships from Chicago only.

products.title: Colombia La Mina Anaerobic
products.body_html:
Origin Story

La Mina may look just like many of the other small farms scattered across the rolling hills of the celebrated Colombian coffee community of Buesaco, but it is hardly common. The López family's selective cherry harvesting, obsessive selection, and meticulous processing have made La Mina one of the country's most decorated coffee farms, with five winning lots (and counting) at the prestigious Cup of Excellence competition. La Mina is the small farm with the big reputation.

Sensory

We are excited to feature an exceptional fruit-forward and jammy anaerobic coffee from La Mina this year, a farm we have been sourcing quality coffee from for many years.

products.title: Guatemala La Maravilla
products.body_html: Growing conditions in Huehuetenango were great this season, but workers were scarce at harvest time. As a result, coffee stayed on the branch longer, and was riper and sweeter when it was picked than in previous years. The elevated ripeness and Mauricio's continued investment in expanding and improving his raised-bed drying allowed us to construct this gem from a careful selection of late-harvest day-lots that express a taste of place, are well-structured and incredibly sweet.

products.title: Kenya Thiriku
products.body_html: Kenya is consistently identified by the most discriminating coffee professionals as the source of some of the world's best and most memorable coffees. And within Kenya, no cooperative has produced more lots that have stood out to our team of coffee professionals than the Thiriku Farmer Cooperative Society.

products.title: Costa Rica Providencia Honey
products.body_html: This exceptional coffee shows what is possible when collaboration throughout the coffee chain is driven by a shared commitment to quality: grown by smallholders farmers in a forest reserve and honey-processed by a cooperative that identifies and markets the very best coffees its members can produce.

products.title: Costa Rica Batamba
products.body_html: This exceptional coffee shows what is possible when collaboration throughout the coffee chain is driven by a shared commitment to quality: the world's most elegant cultivar grown under optimal conditions by a farmer passionate about coffee, and brought to us by a cooperative that identifies and markets the very best coffees its members can produce.

products.title: Honduras Caballero Family
products.body_html: In 2022, we celebrated a landmark — 20 years of collaboration with the Caballero family. In 2023, we celebrate a new start — Fabio and Sandra Isabel Caballero moved into a well-deserved retirement at the end of last season, and passed our relationship on to the next generation of Caballero coffee growers: their daughter, Marysabel, and her husband Moisés. We are in exceptionally good hands, as Marysabel and Moisés are the most decorated coffee growers in the history of the prestigious Honduras Cup of Excellence competition: together they have produced an astounding 14 lots that have reached the CoE finals.

products.title: Ethiopia Washed Buku
products.body_html:
Origin Story

Coffee isn’t merely well-adapted to Ethiopia’s terroir — it evolved in the understory of the majestic forests of what is today Ethiopia. It should come as no surprise, then, that the heirloom varieties still grown there produce flavors that can’t be found anywhere else on earth. And within Ethiopia, we haven’t found anyone producing more flavorful coffees more consistently than the Adinew family operation, METAD. It operates the first CQI-certified lab in Africa and the highly trained teams at its washing stations apply best-in-class quality control processes to create opportunities for thousands of smallholder coffee growers. This lot was grown by members of the Buku Farmers Association and fully washed by METAD at its washing station in Hambela.

Sensory

The washed Buku is a bounty of stone fruit and soft citrus, which is a perfect example of terroir for this coffee.

products.title: Ethiopia Alaka Natural
products.body_html: Grown by smallholders in Guji and processed by our longtime partners at METAD, this lot showcases natural processing at its best. Their meticulous approach preserves the complexity and distinct character that makes Ethiopian coffee unlike any other.

products.title: Costa Rica La Pachuca
products.body_html: We met Roberto Mata back in 2005 when he was leading one of the most successful cooperatives in Central America. Roberto started a new chapter in his coffee story in 2018 when he started a family-owned coffee operation with his wife and children called M+M Pura Vida, which processes and markets coffees from the family's collection of small farms in Tarrazú, including this honey-process lot from his La Pachuca farm.

products.title: Burundi Yandaro
products.body_html: Our coffee team has come to think of Yandaro as the unsung hero of our single origin menu, and Burundi as one of the most underrated coffee origins in the world.

products.title: Bolivia Samaipata Java
products.body_html:
Origin Story

We have been sourcing coffee from Bolivia for more than a decade, virtually all of it from the traditional coffee region of Caranavi in the rugged Andes near the capital La Paz. This coffee comes from the emerging specialty region of Samaipata, near Bolivia's thriving second city Santa Cruz, where the Andes meet the Amazon. This is the second consecutive season we have sourced this Java varietal grown by our oldest direct trade partner in Bolivia, the Rodríguez family.

Sensory

Marked by the playful zing of orange, the homey essence of raw sugar, and the luxuriously smooth undertones of milk chocolate.

products.title: Sublunar Espresso
products.body_html: Our darkest espresso blend, for those who prefer a traditional espresso flavor and larger milk-based drinks. Rich syrup and chocolate notes showcase Sublunar's sweetness, absent of the fruit acidity that define our lighter coffees.

products.title: Bolivia Sol de la Mañana
products.body_html:
Origin Story

We have been sourcing coffee from Bolivia for more than a decade, virtually all of it from the traditional coffee region of Caranavi in the rugged Andes near the capital La Paz. This coffee comes from the emerging specialty region of Samaipata, near Bolivia's thriving second city Santa Cruz, where the Andes meet the Amazon. This is the second consecutive season we have sourced this Java varietal grown by our oldest direct trade partner in Bolivia, the Rodríguez family.

Sensory

Marked by the playful zing of orange, the homey essence of raw sugar, and the luxuriously smooth undertones of milk chocolate.

products.title: Honduras Caballero Family Geisha
products.body_html:
Since 2003, we have been working in Marcala with the Caballero family: Fabio and Sandra Isabel Caballero, their daughter Marysabel, son-in-law Moisés, and the rest of the team at their farms and mills. Since 2012, they have been growing Geisha, the world's most elegant and most celebrated cultivar. This Geisha lot comes from a cool pine grove at Las Virginias, the family's highest-elevation farm.

PLEASE NOTE: This coffee roasts & ships from Chicago only.

products.title: Illumination Blend
products.body_html: This blend is our love letter to the origin of coffee. Ethiopia takes the spotlight in this blend, providing the deep fruit that that embodies the beauty and strength of this iconic coffee region.

products.title: Cold Coffee Blend
products.body_html: From cold brew to flash chill, this blend is curated to love the cold. Bright flavors and fruit notes perform beautifully over ice for year-round cold drinkers who value flavor in a versatile format.

products.title: Organic French Roast Blend
products.body_html: Our darkest roast, with traditional extended roasting that yields semi-sweet, heavy-bodied coffee with a lasting impression.

products.title: Organic Black Cat Espresso
products.body_html: Certified Organic, complex and sweet, this espresso honors the spirit of Black Cat with its added depth and brightness. Grown by forward-thinking producers committed to sustainability — a coffee with both purpose and flavor.

products.title: Intelligentsia's Choice
products.body_html: This monthly rotating subscription will send you a different single origin every month so you can taste the best that each season has to offer. This is a great option for those who like variety and want to explore different origins!

products.title: Intelligentsia House Blend
products.body_html: Bright and lively, House is our benchmark for a light roast blend that showcases fruit and citrus flavors that makeup our favorite coffees.

products.title: Frequency Blend
products.body_html: A crowd pleaser that is versatile and sweet. Frequency is smooth, highlighting flavors of dried fruit and sugar, roasted to achieve consistency and balance.

products.title: El Gato Blend
products.body_html: Black Cat Classic's alter-ego, El Gato embodies the ethos of our Black Cat flagship coffees, designed be brewed as a drip or filter coffee. Perfect for those looking for a comforting cup that delivers subtle fruit accents.

products.title: El Gallo Blend
products.body_html: Morning in a cup, El Gallo is our take on a lighter breakfast blend. Refreshingly smooth, with delicate sweetness and balance that will ease you into your day.
tags: Filter Mug + 12oz El Gallo Breakfast Blend Bundle: 2

products.title: El Diablo Blend
products.body_html: A darker roast that doesn't give up nuance, El Diablo provides a balance of fruit and chocolate showcasing a more developed roast that is approachable and refined.

products.title: Organic Decaf House Blend
products.body_html: Certified Organic and decaffeinated by water process, Organic Decaf House is a must-have for fans of bright filter coffee who value flavor and complexity in their decaf.

products.title: Decaf Black Cat Espresso
products.body_html: Everything you love about Black Cat without the caffeine. This water-processed decaf delivers gentle fruit notes and a sweet, smooth body. Well-suited for any time of day without compromise.

products.title: Black Cat Classic Espresso
products.body_html: Black Cat Classic is our hallmark espresso blend that has been setting the standard in specialty coffee since 1995. Syrupy sweet, with vivid fruit acidity, this blend is our lightest espresso, perfect for purists who seek balance of sweetness and acidity in their shots.

products.title: Black Cat Analog Espresso
products.body_html: Designed to perform in milk-based espresso drinks, Analog produces consistently sweet, chocolate-driven espressos with ease and repeatability. Roasted darker than our Black Cat Classic espresso, Analog is for those that enjoy full-bodied, well-rounded shots with a hint of sweetness.

products.title: Guatemala SL-28
products.body_html: Inspired by the renowned SL-28 variety commonly grown in Kenya, he planted these seeds at La Maravilla to explore how they would adapt to its unique terroir.

products.title: Guatemala Ethiopia Landrace
products.body_html: La Maravilla, perched in the rugged mountains of Huehuetenango, lives up to its name, which means "marvel" in Spanish.

products.title: Kenya Muhathi AA 7oz
products.body_html: We are proud to present this coffee, as it embodies the complexity, resilience, and beauty that define Kenyan coffee.

products.title: Honduras San Isidro Geisha 7oz
products.body_html: The Caballeros have been growing Geisha, the world's most elegant and most celebrated cultivar, since 2012. However, this particular lot represents the first harvest from an area of the farm known as San Isidro.

products.title: Honduras Las Virginias Geisha 7oz
products.body_html: The Caballeros have been growing Geisha, the world's most elegant and most celebrated cultivar, since 2012.

products.title: Brazil Estevão Douro Acauã
products.body_html:
In the highlands of Espírito Santo lies the small town of Marechal Floriano, where Estevão Douro and his family produce coffee on the land where their ancestors first settled after immigrating from Italy to start anew in Brazil. In recent years, with the support of his sons, Denizar and Thiago, Estevão has revitalized the farm by planting new coffee varieties and investing in infrastructure to improve and refine their on-farm processing techniques. This transformation has not only elevated the reputation of their coffee on the international market, but the Douros also offer their own roasted coffee locally.

The farm is home to Acauã, Arara, Catuaí, and Catucaí cultivars, with tomato plants and avocado trees growing alongside them. This particular lot is a selection of Acauã, a hybrid cultivar that has gained popularity in Brazil due to its disease resistance and ability to produce exceptional cup quality. It was sourced from our partners at Osito, who work diligently to discover unique lots from some of Brazil's best smallholder farmers.

products.title: Brazil Edineia Pires Sartori Fioresi 7oz
products.body_html:
In a secluded corner of Bateia, Espírito Santo, Edineia Pires Sartori Fioresi and her husband, Valentim, manage the day-to-day labor of their beloved farm, Recanto Feliz — which translates to "Happy Corner" in English. Of their twelve hectares of land, four are dedicated to coffee. The land size is manageable enough that Edineia and Valentim don't hire outside labor; instead, they opt to harvest and process the farm's production on their own.

The farm is planted with Catuaí, Catucaí, and Paraíso varieties, each cultivated in separate lots. This particular lot is a selection from the farm's Catucaí plants, which produce both yellow and red cherries.

We sourced this coffee from our partners at Osito, who work diligently to find unique lots from some of Brazil's best smallholder farmers.

products.title: Colombia Finca Paraíso Castillo 7oz
products.body_html:
Finca El Paraíso is both a farm and a living laboratory for Diego Bermudez, a coffee producer renowned for his pioneering approach to processing. Initially met with skepticism by some who suspected his coffees might be infused with fruit flavors, Diego has since become a beacon of innovation.

The second of two lots we selected from El Paraíso, this Castillo Tropical lives up to its name, boasting notes of distinctly sweet and aromatic tropical fruits.

The processing of this coffee begins with the harvesting of perfectly-ripe Castillo cherries, which are disinfected and submerged in a tank of water for their first 48-hour fermentation. The coffee is then pulped and fermented for an additional 24 hours, this time with the addition of Kluyveromyces lactis yeast. Commonly used in the production of cheese and other fermented dairy products, this yeast can produce volatile aromatic compounds that are associated with enhanced fruit notes and reduced bitterness.

Near the end of this second fermentation, Diego's thermal shock technique is applied, heating the tank before washing the coffee in cold water—the 'shock' of this cold-water plunge stops the fermentation process. Finally, the coffee is dried in a dehumidifier designed by Diego and his team to ensure that moisture leaves the coffee at a controlled, even pace.

products.title: Colombia Finca Paraíso Geisha 7oz
products.body_html:
Finca El Paraíso is both a farm and a living laboratory for Diego Bermudez, a coffee producer renowned for his pioneering approach to processing. Initially met with skepticism by some who suspected his coffees might be infused with fruit flavors, Diego has since become a beacon of innovation.

One of two lots we selected from El Paraíso, this Geisha Luna offers stunning expressions of both variety and process. The process begins with the selective harvesting of overripe Geisha cherries, which are placed in a tank to undergo their first 12-hour fermentation. The coffee is then pulped and fermented again for 48 hours, with the addition of the sweet, syrupy liquid produced during the first fermentation.

Near the end of this second fermentation, Diego's thermal shock technique is applied, heating the tank before washing the coffee in cold water—the 'shock' of this cold-water plunge stops the fermentation process. Finally, the coffee is dried in a dehumidifier designed by Diego and his team to ensure that moisture leaves the coffee at a controlled, even pace.

Each step in this meticulous process was designed with the Geisha profile and Cauca terroir in mind, enhancing fruit flavors and preserving complexity. The result is a cup bursting with deep purple fruit notes complemented by citric acidity.

products.title: Peru Rayos del Sol Geisha 7oz
products.body_html:
Our second release from Rayos del Sol — and our last single-origin release from Peru until next season — showcases a carefully cultivated Geisha selection from Percy Pintado. Percy's farm, Rayos del Sol, is bordered by his family members who also produce coffee in Alto Ihuamaca, a small town nestled between two forest conservation areas in Peru’s northern highlands. This lot was grown on a portion of the farm dedicated to Geisha and, through the years, it has become a coffee we know and love for its sweet, complex flavors.

In collaboration with our partners at Origin Coffee Lab, we have worked with Rayos del Sol since 2015.

products.title: Peru Rejo Bourbon 7oz
products.body_html: This washed Bourbon is from a collection of individual farms in the Cajamarca region of Peru known as La Palestina. El Rejo is a parcel located at 1950 masl, and is run by the Alarcon family. They reinvest their profits back into the group of farmers, helping to evolve the commodity structure in the community.

products.title: Brazil Santuário Sul Geisha 7oz
products.body_html:
Origin Story

Fazenda Santuário Sul is a coffee nerd's dream farm. Inspired by his travels to Intelligentsia's Extraordinary Coffee Workshops, Luiz Paulo planted over 30 exotic coffee varieties on 80 hectares of land. He has paired his desire for new genetics with a passion for processing. The seeds for this Geisha lot came from Panama which is where this highly sought after variety was (re)discovered in 2004. Luiz Paulo ensured an exceptional cup quality through careful processing. This lot underwent an anaerobic fermentation process for 72 hours before it was dried in a Blue House that is equipped with a special material to reflect harsh wavelengths of light. The result is a slow drying process to ensure a uniform and sweet cup quality.

Sensory

Dried florals and resonant sweetness make this Brazilian geisha harmonious and approachable for all.

products.title: Guatemala Santa Elisa Geisha 7oz
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This lot represents the culmination of a remarkable 10-year reclamation project at Santa Elisa Pachup farm in the Acatenango region of Guatemala. When the owners faced the prospect of renovating 300 hectares of coffee back in 2014, they turned to our friends at Los Volcanes Coffee for help. Los Volcanes financed a staged approach to replanting the farm, committed to purchasing everything it produced, and rebuilt a coffee mill in nearby Antigua damaged in a tropical storm to process the farm’s coffee. In 2018, they established the first Geisha plantation at elevations ranging between 1600 and nearly 1700 meters above sea level. This is the farm’s first Geisha harvest big enough for export, and it is a stunner. Los Volcanes set a little aside for us, and submitted the rest to the Guatemala Cup of Excellence competition, where it took 10th place. We are proud to be the only U.S. roaster to offer this lot.

Sensory

The Santa Elisa Geisha is a delicate balance of sweet and tangy, with its tropical key lime accent that adds a contrast to a subtle floral aftertaste.

products.title: Peru La Palestina Geisha 7oz
products.body_html:
Origin Story

José Alarcón and Zobeida Coronel moved to San José del Alto in 1976 with their four young children to start a fledgling coffee farm. Both the family and the farm have grown over the past 47 years, and today Finca La Palestina is something altogether unique — a sprawling residential compound that is home to three generations of the Alarcón Coronel clan, and a vast coffee farm worked collectively by members of a family focused on quality. This year marks the second Geisha harvest at La Palestina and Intelligentsia’s second year purchasing this lot.

Sensory

Since we started sourcing this coffee in 2022, we have tasted the delicate fruity sweetness with floral undertones evolve year to year - this year is no exception.

products.title: Ethiopia 1931 Gesha Mossto Anaerobic 7oz
products.body_html: The team at Gesha Village is growing some of the oldest cultivars on record near the primeval forests where coffee is believed to have first appeared on earth, but applying thoroughly modern approaches to quality control and innovation. The "mossto anaerobic" process behind this lot involves submerging the coffee seed in its fruit pulp and juice expelled from the coffee cherry in a sealed container for more than three days.

products.title: Mexico Finca Chelín Solok 7oz
products.body_html:
Enrique López of Finca Chelín is not afraid to take risks in his relentless pursuit of flavor. When a friend brought him an obscure seed from Indonesia called Solok that Enrique had never heard of, he didn't flinch, planting it in some of the choicest groves on his farm. This tiny lot represents his first harvest of Solok — and the first we know of anywhere in the world outside Indonesia.

PLEASE NOTE: This coffee roasts & ships from Chicago only.

products.title: Mexico Finca Chelín Hydronatural Natural Geisha
products.body_html:
Origin Story

This lot was grown at Finca Chelín, high in the Sierra Sur of Oaxaca, by Enrique López, a celebrated grower who is among the most experimental coffee farmers in our entire Direct Trade network. It is a single-varietal Geisha, but chances are it won’t taste quite like the last Geisha you tasted. That’s because it is what Enrique calls a “hydronatural natural” lot. Like other naturals, it was dried in the fruit. Unlike other naturals, its slow, four-week drying cycle was interrupted by an overnight soak in cold water at the end of day three. The combination of the coffee’s Geisha genetics, Finca Chelín’s exceptional terroir, and Enrique’s creative processing make this coffee unlike any other Geisha — or any natural — you will taste this year.

products.title: Guatemala La Soledad Geisha 7oz
products.body_html:
Origin Story

What do you get when you take the world's most elegant coffee cultivar to a celebrated coffee region in Guatemala and put it in the hands of a family who knows what to do with it? La Soledad Geisha, a memorable coffee that reflects the hallmark flavors of the cultivar, the terroir of its origin, and the craft of its growers. The Pérez family has been growing coffee at La Soledad, in the volcanic soils of the Acatengango Valley, since 1895. This Geisha lot is an expression of that heritage and the commitment to quality of the fifth-generation growers managing the farm today.

Sensory

This season's geisha from La Soledad in Guatemala is sweet and floral, with an herbaceous note reminiscent of Juniper berries.
